subject: ggplot2 equivalent for 'range' argument of boxplot()

messages.author: 7716e3c39df161e2
messages.subject: ggplot2 equivalent for 'range' argument of boxplot()
parts:
Dear all,

I'm starting to work with ggplot2 and I'd like to mimic the behavior I
get when I set the 'range' argument of graphics::boxplot. The (very
likely trivial) task is:

set.seed(1)
tmp <- data.frame(y=rnorm(1000), x=sample(letters[1:10], 1000, rep=T))
boxplot(y~x, data=tmp, range=0)

What I'm able to do now is restricted to the examples:

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(tmp, aes(y=y, x=x))+geom_boxplot()

but I wasn't able to find any information on ?geom_boxplot that would
help me out on mimicking the 'range' argument...

Thank you very much for any information on this,

With best wishes,

benilton

messages.author: 7716e3c39df161e2
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 equivalent for 'range' argument of boxplot()
parts:
Hi Hadley,

thanks a lot for this. I can use the coef argument to get what I need,
but it (coef) is not totally equivalent to range.

coef works fine for positive values, just like range. The key thing is
that if range is 0, then the whiskers extend to the data extremes. To
get a similar behavior with coef, I need to find a value big enough to
account for all the data points, because if I use 0, all the points
outside the IQR are plotted as outliers.

Thanks,

b
